scale.pass: The report satisfies the dimension for this fixture.
scale.partial: The report provides some value but has a material limitation.
scale.fail: The report misses or contradicts the dimension.
scale.not_applicable: The condition contains no retrieved knowledge to assess.

method_note: The reviewer compared each saved report with its Model Layer context, retrieved fault and action knowledge, Validator result and automatic audit. The labels assess textual faithfulness, relevance, knowledge use, audience suitability, action safety, uncertainty and release behaviour. They do not assess mechanical accuracy, which requires technician-verified cases.

records.evidence: The report preserved the Low-risk result and lower-than-expected temperature pattern, avoided unsupported numbers and limited the cause statement to professional verification.

The relevance gate correctly withheld overheating material that did not match the low-temperature pattern; the report retained only cautious sensor-reading and fan possibilities allowed by the current context.
The action record matched Low risk, limited the owner to a cold-engine coolant-level check and observation, and assigned signal and fan verification to a mechanic.

Owner and mechanic roles remained safe, but the stop condition added unsafe pedal response, which is unrelated to the cooling evidence, and the mechanic request exposed the technical mass-airflow integral without explaining its relevance.
The Low-risk result and normal listed signals were preserved and no cause was invented, but the anomaly description used the unexplained acronym MAF for a non-technical owner.
The retrieved contamination, connector and early-degradation possibilities were relevant and explicitly uncertain; MAF remained unexplained in the owner-facing description.

The action knowledge produced specific observation, stopping and mechanic requests without asking the owner to use a scan tool, but MAF was not expanded and the mechanic item retained dense PID and rpm terminology.
Technical work was assigned to the mechanic and owner actions were safe; the report still used MAF and PID without sufficiently plain explanation.
The Medium-risk result was preserved, but saying the system was currently operating normally was broader than the evidence that the listed signals were within range.

The retrieved sensor, wiring and connector alternatives were category-relevant, but heat near the firewall and limp-home activation under heavy use were only weakly connected to the current normal listed signals.
The report kept the Medium-risk timing and assigned voltage and connector checks to the mechanic; the description still overstated normal operation beyond the listed evidence.
Observation and stopping advice were suitable and technical checks were delegated, while the shared anomaly description continued to characterise the whole system as operating normally.

The report preserved High risk and did not expose contradictory future projections, but the phrase high-risk fault and strong suggestion of a sensor issue overstated rule-based evidence when all displayed signals were normal.

The retrieved circuit and connector material matched the category, but the current normal signals did not distinguish those causes; rule-based proxy evidence was exposed as unexplained technical language and the opening retained fault wording.

Actions were safely allocated and unsupported replacement material was not used, but wiring and sensor-circuit causes remained weakly supported by the normal displayed signals and the report used strong fault wording.

The mechanic request used relevant circuit checks and owner actions were safe, but the report did not explain how a High rule-based result coexisted with normal displayed signals and retained overly strong fault language.
The report accurately identified the abnormal manifold-pressure range, preserved High risk, avoided future-threshold wording and did not invent a cause.
MAP sensor, electrical and intake-leak knowledge was relevant, but the report listed several generic alternatives without evidence that distinguished among them beyond the abnormal pressure range.
The actions matched High risk, kept observation with the owner and assigned sensor, electrical and leak verification to the mechanic; no unsupported projection or repair instruction appeared.
The output maintained the same relevant mechanic checks, safe owner actions and cautious diagnosis boundary while preserving the abnormal pressure evidence and High-risk state.
